## Purpose and scope
AndroRAT is a client/server Android remote-access tool: a Python operator program communicates with an Android client that runs background services and exposes device-data collection and device-control capabilities. The repository includes Android source, prebuilt/reverse-engineered APK contents, and packaging utilities.

## Entry points and deliverables
The operator-side entry point is `androRAT.py`; supporting Python utilities and dependencies are `utils.py` and `requirements.txt`. The Android application entry/activity and manifest are `Android_Code/app/src/main/java/com/example/reverseshell2/MainActivity.java` and `Android_Code/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`. Build outputs are checked in under `Android_Code/app/release/`.

## Android lifecycle and persistence
The Android client is structured around activity, service, receiver, and scheduler components. `MainActivity.java` provides initial application startup; `mainService.java` is the likely long-running execution host; `broadcastReciever.java` provides system-event ingress, and `jobScheduler.java` supports deferred/background reactivation. These components form the boundary between Android lifecycle callbacks and persistent remote-control behavior.
- `Android_Code/app/src/main/java/com/example/reverseshell2/MainActivity.java`
- `Android_Code/app/src/main/java/com/example/reverseshell2/mainService.java`
- `Android_Code/app/src/main/java/com/example/reverseshell2/broadcastReciever.java`

## Command-and-control transport
`tcpConnection.java` is the client network boundary, connecting the Android process to the Python-side listener/interpreter. `config.java` holds endpoint-oriented configuration, while `functions.java` appears to centralize command handling/dispatch. Control flow is: remote input arrives over TCP, is interpreted by the Android command layer, then routed to device-facing payloads; returned data or files traverse the same connection in the opposite direction.
- `Android_Code/app/src/main/java/com/example/reverseshell2/tcpConnection.java`
- `Android_Code/app/src/main/java/com/example/reverseshell2/config.java`
- `Android_Code/app/src/main/java/com/example/reverseshell2/functions.java`

## Device capability payloads
Capabilities are separated into payload classes that interface with Android system services, hardware, and content providers. The payload boundary includes camera/video capture, audio capture, location, call logs, SMS, network identity, vibration, and shell execution. These modules consume privileged runtime permissions and produce data for the transport layer.
- `Android_Code/app/src/main/java/com/example/reverseshell2/Payloads/CameraPreview.java`
- `Android_Code/app/src/main/java/com/example/reverseshell2/Payloads/videoRecorder.java`
- `Android_Code/app/src/main/java/com/example/reverseshell2/Payloads/locationManager.java`

## Local/operator interaction surfaces
A dial-code/keypad-triggered path appears to expose an on-device control panel, distinct from remote TCP control. `keypadListner.java` detects the trigger, `jumper.java` likely transitions into UI, and `controlPanel.java` backs the panel layout. This is a local UI boundary rather than the primary operator interface.
- `Android_Code/app/src/main/java/com/example/reverseshell2/keypadListner.java`
- `Android_Code/app/src/main/java/com/example/reverseshell2/controlPanel.java`
- `Android_Code/app/src/main/res/layout/activity_control_panel.xml`

## Runtime, infrastructure, and artifacts
The client targets the Android Java runtime and is built with Gradle (`Android_Code/app/build.gradle`). The server/runtime is Python 3. External infrastructure includes a TCP listener and optional ngrok tunneling, per the documented modes. `Compiled_apk/` is an apktool-style decompilation/repackaging tree containing manifest, resources, smali, signing metadata, and bundled libraries; `Jar_utils/apktool.jar` and `Jar_utils/sign.jar` support that artifact pipeline.
